obligation: Report actual or threatened cyber incident (Coast Guard, FBI, CISA)
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering the terminal, including its data, networks and systems (for example a ransom note, encryption of TOS or gate servers, or a compromised VPN account)
notify: FBI (local field office), CISA (cisa.gov/report) and the Captain of the Port (Coast Guard Sector command center; number in the FSP and incident binder)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the terminal is a waterfront facility with an FSP under 33 CFR Part 105. CySO reports; FSO if the CySO cannot be reached

obligation: Reportable cyber incident to the National Response Center (fallback)
trigger: A reportable cyber incident (for example substantial loss of availability of a covered system, or disruption of business operations) that has not been reported to the Coast Guard under 6.16-1
applies_at_this_tier: Only if no report was made under 6.16-1. A 6.16-1 report to the Coast Guard satisfies this duty

trigger: Activities that may result in a transportation security incident (for example signs that attackers are targeting PACS, CCTV or crane controllers)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FSO decides under the FSP

citation: 33 CFR 101.305(b); breach of security defined in 101.105
trigger: Security measures circumvented, eluded or violated without a TSI (for example TWIC access control or CCTV disabled by the attack)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if FSP security measures are affected - FSO decides

trigger: A security incident resulting in significant loss of life, environmental damage, transportation system disruption or economic disruption in the area
deadline: Without delay, then follow the FSP procedures
notify: Captain of the Port (the FSP may also call for the National Response Center)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the outage reaches TSI level (for example a multi-day terminal closure) - FSO and General Manager decide with the COTP

trigger: Any reportable cyber incident or cyber threat
deadline: Create during the incident; keep at least 2 years, protected from unauthorized deletion or amendment
notify: FSO records system; CySO reports the incident to the owner or operator

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example employee records, or truck driver names with driver license numbers held in the TOS gate module)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information was accessed - Finance and Administration Manager with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example the TOS vendor portal or the payroll provider) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company within 10 days of determining the breach
notify: The company (Finance and Administration Manager); the company then gives the notices above

trigger: Affected truck drivers or employees who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected individuals; apply the law of each state where they reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: TOS vendor incident notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Security incident at the TOS vendor affecting the hosted portal or remote support
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. Subpart F requires vendors to notify without delay (101.650(f)(2)); contracts to be updated (POAM-024)

obligation: Carriers, port authority and other port partners
citation: Terminal services agreements; port lease; data exchange agreements (contracts)
trigger: Incident affecting vessel operations, the gate, or data exchanged with partners
deadline: Per each agreement; operationally as soon as EDI or the gate is suspended
notify: Ocean carriers with vessels due; port authority; port community system; customs data exchange service; trucking companies (portal notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational. Check notice clauses in each agreement

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated rail, transit or pipeline operator
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a rail, transit or pipeline operator (N48-49-R02, R03)

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within four business days after determining materiality

trigger: Covered equipment or Kaspersky article found in use
deadline: Within 1 business day (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
